128568.overview:
Tiny necklace type of game, with built-in stopwatch.
This is a foreign Ludotronic release: Colere au Tennis.

128571.overview: TRON is a handheld game released by Tomy in 1982. It consists of three games that are based on action sequences from the movie TRON. In the first game, the player must move his light cycle around the Game Grid to cut off three Warrior Elite light cycles one at a time. In the second game, Tron and Sark, throw discs at each other in the hope that either of them will miss catching it, causing that player to lose one of his four bars, the game being a combination of the jai-alai ring game from the movie and the arcade game Pong. In the third game, the player must throw his disc into the heart of the MCP to destroy it once and for all. Once all three games have been completed, the cycle starts anew with a faster and higher level of difficulty.

129201.overview:
Ball (originally known as Toss-Up in North America) is a Game & Watch game released as a part of the Silver series on April 28, 1980. It was the first Game & Watch game. It is a single-screen single-player Game & Watch.

In Game A, the player tosses two balls in the air. As the balls fall, the player must catch and toss them up again. One point is earned for each successful catch. A dropped ball will display a broken ball and end the game. The object is to continuously catch the balls that fall and throw them back up. In Game B, the player must juggle three balls, and each successful catch rewards ten points instead of one.

The highest possible score a user can obtain is 9,999 for Game A and 9,990 for Game B, due to 9,999 not being a multiple of 10.

Input: Left button (controls character's arms as well as the hours on the clock), right button (controls character's arm as well as the minutes on the clock), Game A button, Game B button, Time button (displays time), ACL (allows user to change the time displayed).

129203.overview:
The player receives items and must cross a bridge of five turtles to deliver the items to the receiver on the other side of a lake. Each time the player delivers an item, they earn three points. On the way back to the home bank to grab the next item, the player earns from two to 12 extra points depending on how fast they return. However, the turtles at times will go down into the lake to eat fish, and if the player jumps onto or stays on a descending turtle, that player will fall into the lake and lose a life. Also, the player might need to wait for the receiver to appear and cannot return to the home bank while carrying an item. If the player reaches 200 or 500 points without any misses, then no fish will appear for the turtles for 20 to 40 seconds. If the player has any misses at either score, every miss will be cleared instead. The player receives a Game Over when they lose three lives.

In Game A, most fish appear to the left and right of the center turtle, and it does not descend unless the player stays on it too long. In Game B, however, fish will appear more frequently for the center turtle.

147987.overview: Tom & Jerry Prank is a vintage electronic LCD handheld game released in 1983 by Gakken. It features classic cat-and-mouse gameplay where players must help Tom catch a mischievous Jerry while avoiding traps.

147989.overview: 1981 Gakken TOWERING RESCUE Vintage LCD Electronic Handheld Video Game and Watch.

149248.overview:
The Tom & Jerry Popper is a rare, vintage handheld electronic LCD card game released in 1983 by the Japanese company Gakken. Part of Gakken's ultra-slim "Card Game" series, it featured licensed characters from the classic Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer (MGM) cartoon.

Tom flies balloon bombs across the screen, and the player must use a saber to pop them quickly.You control a character at the bottom center of the screen. A mistake is triggered if you fail to pop the balloons or if a magnet steals your saber (exclusive to Game B mode).The game ends after 3 mistakes.

162013.overview: The player controls a man who holds up a fishbowl to catch fish that jump from a fish tank. The player needs to keep catching the fish to transfer them to the other fish tank on the other side. Each time a fish lands in the fishbowl or the other fish tank, the player receives a point. As the player progresses in the game, more fish will appear, and they will eventually jump faster. If a fish lands on the floor, a cat will eat it and spit out the bones, and the player will get a miss. At 300 points, any misses the player has will be removed. The player receives a Game Over when they have three misses. In Game A, fish jump from the right fish tank to the left one. In Game B, fish might jump from either fish tank, and they also might jump either right or left after landing in the fishbowl.

190415.overview: Ninja Gaiden is a handheld LCD electronic video game developed by Tiger Electronics, based on Tecmo's Ninja Gaiden arcade game.

190418.overview: Robocop 2 is a handheld LCD electronic video game developed by Tiger Electronics, based on the movie Robocop 2 from 1990.

190421.overview: The Shadow is a handheld LCD electronic video game developed by Tiger Electronics, based on the movie The Shadow from 1994.

190425.overview: Space Harrier II is a handheld LCD electronic video game developed by Tiger Electronics, based on Sega's Space Harrier II arcade game.

190427.overview: Spider-Man is a handheld LCD electronic video game developed by Tiger Electronics.

190432.overview:
In Transformers: Generation 2, Optimus Prime leads the Autobots in a renewed battle against the Decepticons for control of Earth. As Decepticon forces descend from the skies under Starscream’s command, the player must defend Autobot territory, transform between robot and vehicle modes, and eliminate the enemy threat before time runs out.

Players control Optimus Prime through a side-view battlefield that alternates between open terrain and enemy airspace. The directional pad moves the character left and right or shifts between ground and elevated positions. The two action buttons—Call/Transform and Attack—govern transformation and combat.

Each mode offers tactical trade-offs: the truck form moves faster and avoids incoming fire more easily, while the robot form can shoot upward to intercept airborne enemies. Collectible icons represented by “P” along the screen bottom provide weapon power-ups.

190435.overview: X-Men is a handheld LCD electronic video game developed by Tiger Electronics.

190451.overview:
The Tamagotchi is a handheld digital pet that was created in Japan by Akihiro Yokoi of WiZ and Aki Maita of Bandai. It was released by Bandai on November 23, 1996 in Japan and on May 1, 1997 in the rest of the world, quickly becoming one of the biggest toy fads of the late 1990s and the early 2000s.

Upon activating the toy, an egg appears on the screen. After setting the clock on the device, the egg will wiggle for several minutes, and then hatch into a small pet. In later versions, inputting the player's name and birthday is also required when setting the clock, and at birth, the player can name the pet and learn of its family group and/or gender. The player can care for the pet as much or as little as they choose, and the outcome depends on the player's actions. The first Tamagotchis could only be paused by going to set the clock, effectively stopping the passage of time in the game, but in later models a pause function was included.

190467.overview: The object of the game is to get a high score maneuvering the caveman to steal the egg while skillfully evading volcanic bombs, dinosaur attacks, and interference from a dragon.

190468.overview: Your mission is to blast the aliens out of the sky while avoiding their attacking bombs, to score the maximum points possible of 999.

190497.overview:
Atari's first (and only released) handheld game. This is a handheld version of Atari's Touch Me arcade game (which was released in 1974), and it's the game that Milton Bradley got the idea for Simon from (it's the exact same game, just bigger).

Touch Me is a one to four-player game where your memory and your concentration are the most important factors. There are three games, each one similar, yet slightly different. The object in all of the games generally speaking, is to follow the sequence of flashing lights or "signals" by pressing corresponding colored buttons. Each signal is accompanied by one of four different electronic tones.

206476.overview: An LCD game based on same hardware as Tronica's Space Rescue but with a submarine theme instead of space shuttle.

206754.overview: A one or two player Tennis Game. Three difficulty settings when choosing single play.

210821.overview: You are at the helm of Air Traffic Control. You must successfully navigate several planes through take off and landings with as few crashes as possible.

423404.overview:
A handheld from Tandy. You are able to switch between Football, Soccer, and Basketball via interchangeable face plates. 

-3 separate, easy-to-change playing field inserts
-Exciting 2-player action in 3 games
-2 skill levels on each game
-LED scoreboard display
-Pass and Shoot plus Angle Pass and Shoot controls

462406.overview:
Turtles places the player in control of a small turtle navigating a glowing labyrinth while rescuing baby turtles hidden beneath mysterious boxes. Enemy beetles roam the maze, and only quick movement and clever use of bombs can keep the rescuer alive long enough to deliver the babies to safety.

Players move their turtle one step at a time using the left joystick to navigate corridors, revealing what’s hidden beneath each “?” box. Some conceal baby turtles who cling to the player’s shell, while others release enemy beetles that immediately begin pursuit.

The goal is to transport all rescued turtles to the home nests located around the maze without being caught. Pressing the right-hand orange button drops a bomb, stunning nearby enemies for a moment—an essential tactic in later stages.

467071.overview:
The Tandy Stack Challenge (also branded as the Radio Shack Stack Challenge, Model 60-2247) is a vintage handheld electronic LCD game released in 1991 that functions as an unofficial Tetris clone. Produced by Tandy Corporation and sold through Radio Shack retail stores, the device became a popular retro gaming staple due to its unique physical design and surprisingly robust audio.

While it plays identical to classic Tetris, this version is widely considered by retro enthusiasts to be uniquely difficult due to a highly aggressive random block generation algorithm.

476921.overview:
Tom and Jerry, the mischievous cat and mouse team, are about to go on their greatest adventure! Their friend, Robyn Starling, has become a victim of a kidnapping caper! Robyn's mean old Aunt Figg will do anything to try and get her hands on Robyn's inheritance, but she has to find a way to do it! When Robyn runs away from her Aunt with Tom and Jerry, a whole whirlwind of events takes place! Help Tom and Jerry and Robyn escape the clutches of Aunt Figg, Captain Kiddie, the Straycatchers and the horrible dog, Ferdinand! The last stage will lead you to a carnival, where you must help Robyn get rescued by her father before it's too late!

Help Tom and Jerry pick up a manhole cover so the evil Straycatchers will fall in before they get you!

Save Robyn from the burning door before the kidnappers come!

Finally, Robyn has been rescued by her father with the help of her friends Tom and Jerry, and of course, you!

477663.overview:
The evil Drakkus has changed his name to Berserko and is out to get his revenge on our "heroes on the half-shell" by destroying the Earth! Not a chance! These Turtles have an attitude! Clever, cooler and edgier than ever, they're ready to kick some butt! Use your Ninja moves and special weapons to put Berserko, Bebop and Rocksteady in their place! Power up on some pizza when you grab a bite! Best of all, you get to hear the awesome voices of your favorite dudes while you play! Cowabunga!

COOL DUDE! YOU CAN CHOOSE THE TURTLE OF YOUR CHOICE TO BATTLE THE BAD GUYS!

AWESOME! PIZZA SLICES WILL APPEAR ON SCREEN - YOU HAVE TO SCARF 'EM UP TO REPLENISH YOUR ENERGY!

WHOA! WATCH OUT FOR BEBOP AND ROCKSTEADY. THEY'RE SOME DANGEROUS DUDES. SHOW EM SOME ATTITUDE WITH A NINJA KICK OR USE YOUR NINJA FIGHTING WEAPON!

478695.overview:
Players navigate basic, repetitive action loops trying to rack up points while avoiding obstacles in signature Beavis and Butt-Head fashion.
Talking Feature: Unlike standard silent LCD units of the era, this version included a sound chip capable of producing low-bitrate voice clips and sound effects matching the show's crude tone.
Controls: Basic directional pad and action buttons typical of 1990s Tiger handhelds.

478747.overview:
You call the plays, throw the passes, run the ball and make the tackles. Select your team, plan your offensive or defensive strategy, and play it out. Realistic football action ... 4 quarters with running, tackles, passes, kicking, field goals, and touchdowns. Display shows downs/yards, field position, time, quarter, and score.

Choose from these twelve teams: Indianapolis, Miami, Cleveland, Denver, Seattle, Los Angeles, Washington, San Francisco, Dallas, New York, Chicago, and Minnesota.

Watch your energy bar to control the kickoff.

Whether you are offense or defense, you select the formation.

Go for the Field Goal! Direct the ball and watch the kick meter.

The defense is protecting the line, but with great concentration and fast feet- TOUCHDOWN! and now try for the extra point.

478875.overview:
Taz is on a food hunt and needs your help to get as much as he can!
Call on Dog the Turtle and Constance Koala to help!
Watch out for Bull Gator and his sidekick Axl. They want to get the food before Taz does!
Steer Taz clear of obstacles by using his super-fast spin.

482406.overview: A diver descends from a boat to gather treasure guarded by a giant octopus. Watch the tentacles extend and withdraw, choose a safe route to the seabed and return with the loot. Going farther promises more points but creates a longer journey back through danger. This Elektronika handheld follows the treasure-diving mechanics of Game & Watch Octopus.
